intro: Suggestions raised by this session. Nothing here has been implemented. Each one lists the paths that were considered and a recommendation, so the choice can be made before any code changes. Items marked 'owner decision' touch a file another session owns; they are logged as change requests in COORDINATION.md rather than executed here.

suggestions.title: Decide how the dashboard picks the injury snapshot it publishes
suggestions.problem: The site publishes the 05:15 AM ET report while a 1:30 PM ET report exists. The gap is 8h15m and 24 report versions, and it spans the league's game-day filing window.
paths: A. Repoint data/app/snapshot_manifest.json at the newest capture each time one is taken (smallest change; the capture stays a deliberate act).
B. Keep the current snapshot and add a report-age badge to every page that uses it (honest, but the stale numbers stay on screen).
C. Add a scheduled workflow that re-captures the report every 15 minutes and rebuilds (freshest, but it breaks the byte-reproducibility the CI drift gate depends on unless the artefact is pinned).
suggestions.recommendation: A now, C later with a pinned artefact. B is a fallback if the rebuild cost is a concern.

suggestions.title: Stop storing the availability verdict as a boolean in a file
suggestions.problem: data/app/report_availability.json stores deadline_passed_at_capture computed against one report. Four teams have since filed, and because the engine reads that file, out_players_* shows the new names while out_count_* and availability_state_* stay blank.
paths: A. Recompute the file from the newest report on every refresh (one-line fix, same failure mode next time).
B. Derive the state inside strategy_lab.py from the report it is already reading, so the two can never disagree (removes the class of bug; needs a report timestamp in the artefact).
C. Leave it and document the split (cheapest; the disagreement stays visible on the page).
suggestions.recommendation: B. Two published fields that contradict each other is worse than either value being stale.

suggestions.title: Decide whether injuries should ever move a line
suggestions.problem: The engine prices from ratings, rest and pace. Injuries are published next to the line but never in it, so Cleveland filing with Mitchell and Harden Questionable and Mobley Out changes nothing.
paths: A. Leave it injury-blind and say so on the lines page (honest; zero risk of a bad adjustment).
B. Publish a second, clearly labelled injury-shadow line next to the model line, using only the minutes table we hold (shows the size of the gap without pretending it is validated).
C. Fit a minutes-to-value coefficient out of sample and gate it like every other strategy (the only path that earns a real adjustment; it needs the data in Q-1823b910-02 first).
suggestions.recommendation: A today, B as a labelled experiment, C only after the per-player capture exists and the coefficient survives the nine gates.

suggestions.title: Extend the official per-player minutes capture
suggestions.problem: The minutes vacuum is a floor of 0 for nine of the ten 11/14 team-games, because only 31 players have a captured official minutes figure.
paths: A. Capture the top 100 by minutes per game (one fetch, covers most rotation players).
B. Capture the full per-player traditional table (largest artefact, covers everyone including two-way players).
C. Leave it at 31 and keep publishing the floor.
suggestions.recommendation: A. It converts most of the zeros into real numbers at a modest artefact cost; B can follow if two-way players turn out to matter.

suggestions.title: Publish the age of every official snapshot on the page that uses it
suggestions.problem: The dashboard says which report it used in the data, but a reader has to go looking. The 8h15m gap was invisible until this session re-read the index.
paths: A. One 'data as of' line in the site header, driven by the snapshot manifest.
B. A per-page badge showing the age of each official source that page uses.
C. A freshness page listing every capture and its age (the repository has one; it is not linked from the landing page).
suggestions.recommendation: A plus C. The freshness page already exists and only needs a link.
suggestions.decision_needed: Owner of scripts/build_app.py and the landing page.

suggestions.title: Schedule the injury capture as a job instead of a session task
suggestions.problem: Every report refresh so far has been done by whichever agent session happened to be running. The report changes every 15 minutes; the refresh should not depend on that.
paths: A. A scheduled GitHub Action that captures the newest report and opens a pull request (reviewable, no auto-merge).
B. A scheduled Action that captures and commits straight to main (freshest; bypasses review).
suggestions.recommendation: A. It keeps the standing rule that a human chooses before anything changes, while removing the dependence on a session being open.
